thread:
jules-eng: Hey @erin-peopleops — edge case. I'm on extended medical LOA that spans Nov-Dec. My return date is Jan 10. Company shutdown Dec 24-27 is during my LOA. Do those shutdown days count against my PTO carryover or are they treated as LOA-protected? I'm trying to plan for 2026 accruals.

erin-peopleops: Short answer: we treat company shutdowns differently depending on LOA type and country. For medical LOA approved under the company's leave policy, shutdown days that fall entirely during LOA are normally marked as 'LOA-covered shutdown' and do not consume PTO. But we need the LOA record + manager confirmation.

jules-eng: Good to know. My case: approved FMLA-style medical LOA, HR case #HR-LOA-2025-112. Will that be enough?

tara-hr: Yes that helps. We also need payroll jurisdiction and whether time is unpaid or paid LOA. If unpaid LOA, shutdown days are still usually marked as company shutdown credits so you don't lose future accruals, but benefits continuity rules may differ. Share the LOA approval doc in the portal and we'll tag it.

jules-eng: I'm US-payrolled, unpaid medical LOA. Submitted LOA docs into People Portal and linked HR case HR-LOA-2025-112.

erin-peopleops: Thanks. Steps we follow: 1) Confirm LOA type and payroll journal 2) Manager sign-off that employee is still on approved LOA during shutdown 3) People Ops marks shutdown days as 'LOA-protected shutdown' which does not deduct PTO and does not change carryover limits.

matt-mgr: Confirming Jules is on approved LOA for that period. Approving exception.

erin-peopleops: Legal check: @legal-bot, any constraints for unpaid medical LOA and shutdown credits for US employees?

legal-bot: Quick policy lookup: for US FMLA-type leave, employer may not require use of accrued PTO during leave unless specified. Company policy permits marking shutdown as non-deductible for approved medical LOA. Ensure consistent application and document in employee record.

jules-eng: Great. Will I see any change to my 2026 accrual cap or carryover limits? My concern is carryover max is 10 days and I was saving PTO to carry over.

erin-peopleops: Because we mark these as LOA-protected shutdown credits, they do not count as used PTO. They also do not count as an extra accrual, so your carryover calculation stays based on actual accrued and used PTO. If you want to preserve carryover, we recommend returning early enough to have accruals reflected before year cutoff, but policy doesn't penalize LOA.

jules-eng: Ok thanks. One more: if the LOA extends into next year and I return mid-Jan, can I request an exception to front-load accruals to cover missed time?

tara-hr: We don't front-load future accruals except in rare cases (e.g., approved medical hardship). That requires manager + HR + finance sign-off. If you think you'll need override, open a People Portal ticket -> Leave Exceptions -> "Accrual Front-load Request" and attach medical docs.

erin-peopleops: Jules, to close this ticket I'll mark EX-2026-4012 as 'LOA-protected shutdown approved' and attach notes. You'll get a DM with the record.

jules-eng: Thanks all 64f Appreciate the clarity.

erin-peopleops: Done 4dd EX-2026-4012 updated and approved by matt-mgr at 1912345805. We'll add the LOA note to payroll so carryover calc remains intact.

tara-hr: If anyone else is on LOA spanning shutdowns, please batch requests so payroll updates can be applied together (avoid multiple cutoff exceptions).

jules-eng: Will do. Thanks everyone.
